topic.name: Solving Equations With Odd Exponents Using the Nth Root Method

question.text: Find the real solution to the equation $2(x+4)^3 = 686.$
question.explanation:
We can solve this equation by isolating the $(x+4)^3$ term and then taking the $3$rd root of each side.

First, let's isolate the $(x+4)^3$ term on the left-hand side:

\begin{align} 2(x+4)^3 &= 686 \\[3pt] (x+4)^3 &= 343 \end{align}

Now, we take the $3$rd root of each side and solve for $x.$ Since $n=3$ is odd, there is only one real solution to this equation:

\begin{align} (x+4)^3 &= 343 \\[3pt] \sqrt[3]{(x+4)^3} &= \sqrt[3]{343} \\[3pt] x+4 &= \sqrt[3]{7^3} \\[3pt] x+4 &= 7 \\[3pt] x &= 3 \end{align}

Therefore, the solution is $x=3.$

example.title: Solving Equations Containing an Expression Raised to an Odd Power

question.text: Find the real solution to the equation $x^7=-\dfrac{1}{128}.$
question.explanation:
We can solve this equation by taking the $7$th root of each side and solving for $x.$ Since $n=7$ is odd, there is only one real solution to this equation:

\begin{align} x^7 &= -\dfrac{1}{128} \\[3pt] \sqrt[7]{x^7} &= \sqrt[7]{\left(-\dfrac{1}{128}\right)} \\[3pt] x &= \sqrt[7]{\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^7} \\[3pt] x &= -\dfrac12 \end{align}

Therefore, the solution is $x=-\dfrac12.$

question.text: Find the real solution to the equation $(x-3)^7 = -128.$
question.explanation:
We can solve this equation by taking the $7$th root of each side and solving for $x.$ Since $n=7$ is odd, there is only one real solution to this equation:

\begin{align} (x-3)^7 &= -128 \\[3pt] \sqrt[7]{(x-3)^7} &= \sqrt[7]{-128} \\[3pt] x-3 &= \sqrt[7]{(-2)^7} \\[3pt] x-3 &= -2 \\[3pt] x &= 1 \end{align}

Therefore, the solution is $x=1.$
